# Cantrip.Syntax

The syntax tree the parser builds. A game never touches it; a tool that reads content lives in it.

Part of [the API reference](README.md). The guides are [docs/csharp.md](../csharp.md) and [docs/godot.md](../godot.md); when something here surprises you, [docs/troubleshooting.md](../troubleshooting.md) is the other end of it.

## Lexer

```csharp
public sealed class Lexer
```

Turns DSL source text into a token stream with explicit `TokenKind.Indent`/`TokenKind.Dedent` tokens.

Blocks are indentation-delimited, so the parser never has to guess where a listener body ends. Blank lines and comment-only lines produce no tokens at all, which means a designer can space content out freely without changing its meaning.

### Constructors

```csharp
public Lexer(string text, string file, DiagnosticBag diagnostics)
```

*Undocumented.*


## Parser

```csharp
public sealed class Parser
```

Recursive-descent parser for the effects DSL.

The grammar is deliberately shallow. Statements are parsed as a verb name followed by positional arguments and named clauses (`to`, `from`, `for`, ...), and the parser attaches no meaning to any of them. Verb semantics live in the interpreter's verb registry, so content can add verbs without the grammar growing a case for each one.

### Constructors

```csharp
public Parser(IReadOnlyList<Token> tokens, string file, DiagnosticBag diagnostics)
```

*Undocumented.*

### Properties

```csharp
public static IReadOnlyList<string> ClauseWords { get; }
```

Words that introduce a named clause and therefore terminate the argument list. These are the only reserved words inside a command line.

This is grammar, not meaning: the parser still attaches none to any of them, and which verb reads which is `BuiltinClauses`'s business. Four of these words — `at`, `over`, `against` and `using` — are read by no built-in verb and stay that way. They are here so that a verb a game registers in C# can read them, and so that a built-in verb handed one can name the word that works instead.

### Methods

```csharp
public static bool IsClauseWord(string word)
```

True for a word that introduces a clause, as opposed to a flag written after a comma.

```csharp
public static SourceFileNode Parse(string text, string file, DiagnosticBag diagnostics)
```

*Undocumented.*

```csharp
public ExprNode ParseExpression()
```

*Undocumented.*

```csharp
public SourceFileNode ParseFile()
```
